about: Per-target MCP compatibility statements for the next public audits, from the preflight (evidence/mcp-preflight/*.json) and the pinned packages' own sources. SUPPORTED: measured through RigorRun's client. PARTIAL: protocol-compatible by the target's own source, not measured here; the listed preconditions are mandatory before any finding is attributed upstream. UNSUPPORTED / UNKNOWN would fail GATE 9.

rigorrunClient.2026-07-28: UNSUPPORTED (client side); a server that speaks only 2026-07-28 is refused at connect with a visible error and no case runs (evidence: modern-only-server.json)

targets.name: Filesystem MCP
preconditions: record the negotiated protocol version from a raw handshake (RigorRun records "negotiated" for stdio)

targets.name: GitHub MCP
targets.serverProtocol: dual-era: go-sdk v1.7.0 supports 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05, and answers the legacy initialize handshake capped at 2025-11-25
preconditions: pin the server build and record the negotiated version from a raw initialize handshake (expected 2025-11-25)
compare RigorRun's discovered tool count with a raw paged tools/list; go-sdk's default page size is 1000, but RigorRun ignores nextCursor, so any second page would be invisible

prefer the stdio binary or container with the token in the environment; the remote HTTP endpoint needs a secret literally named Authorization, and every project secret is handed to every connector, verifier included
reproduce any timeout with a raw client before attributing it upstream

targets.name: Playwright MCP
targets.serverProtocol: legacy: the MCP SDK bundled in playwright-core declares LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2025-11-25; no 2026-07-28 support in the package
preconditions: record the negotiated version and a raw paged tools/list count before the audit

measure the server's stderr volume with a raw client: RigorRun pipes stderr and never reads it, and 200 KB stalled both calls (stderr-flood.json); any TIMED_OUT must be reproduced with a raw client before it is called an upstream failure

browser tool results are prose snapshots and images, which normalise to text or empty: verdicts must rest on an independent verifier read (a separate process reading browser or application state), never on the tools' own results
raise toolCallMs for browser actions that can exceed the 20 s default, keeping caseMs >= toolCallMs + 5000
